key_insight: Zero-shot deep local-feature matching achieves near-perfect photographic re-identification of the Hula painted frog without species-specific training, outperforming deep global-feature embedding approaches.
problem_solved: Enables non-invasive, accurate individual identification for a critically endangered amphibian (Hula painted frog) where physical marking is impractical or harmful.
method: Dataset: 1,233 ventral images from 191 known individuals collected during 2013–2020 capture–recapture surveys.
Approach: zero-shot deep local-feature matching — extract dense local descriptors, match keypoints across images, and spatially verify correspondences to declare identity matches.
Comparison: evaluated against deep global-feature embedding (re‑id) models using identification metrics (top‑1/top‑k accuracy, false positives) to show superior performance of local matching.
impact: Demonstrates that zero-shot local-feature methods can solve fine-grained re-identification with minimal annotation, reducing data/label requirements and providing a transferable pipeline for wildlife monitoring and other re‑ID problems.
